```plato
//==
// # Skeletal animation
//
// Sections, in order:
//  - Skeletal animation
//  - IProcedural rig control

//==
// # Skeletal animation
//
// The rig and the data bound to it: bones, skeletons, poses, skin weights,
// morph targets, sockets, and skeletal clips. Bones form a forest addressed by
// index into the owning skeleton's bone array; -1 is the "no bone" sentinel
// throughout. Poses are local: each bone's pose is expressed relative to its
// parent (roots relative to the model).

// A zero-based index of a bone within the owning skeleton's bone array.
// -1 means "no bone".
type BoneIndex
    implements IValue, IHashable, IComparable, IIndex
{
    Value: Integer;
}

// A named node in a skeleton hierarchy. Parent indexes the owning skeleton's
// bone array; -1 marks a root. BindPose is the bone's rest pose relative to its
// parent (relative to the model for roots).
type Bone
    implements IValue
{
    Name: String;
    Parent: BoneIndex;
    BindPose: Pose3D;
}

// An ordered array of bones forming a forest. Bones are topologically ordered:
// every bone's Parent index is less than its own index, so a single forward
// pass composes local poses into model space.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skeletal_animation)
type Skeleton
    implements IValue
{
    Bones: Array<Bone>;
}

// A full articulation of a skeleton: one local pose per bone, parallel to the
// owning skeleton's bone array. Composing along parent chains yields
// model-space poses (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forward_kinematics).
type SkeletonPose
    implements IValue
{
    LocalPoses: Array<Pose3D>;
}

// One bone's influence on a vertex: the bone's index in the skeleton and the
// blend weight of its transform.
type SkinWeight
    implements IValue
{
    Bone: BoneIndex;
    Weight: Proportion;
}

// All bone influences on a single vertex. Weights sum to 1; renderers commonly
// keep the four largest.
type VertexSkinWeights
    implements IValue
{
    Weights: Array<SkinWeight>;
}

// Binds a mesh to a skeleton for linear-blend skinning. InverseBindTransforms
// is parallel to the skeleton's bones and carries each bone's inverse
// model-space bind transform; VertexWeights is parallel to the mesh's vertices.
type SkinBinding
    implements IValue
{
    Skeleton: Skeleton;
    InverseBindTransforms: Array<AffineTransform3D>;
    VertexWeights: Array<VertexSkinWeights>;
}

// A named blend-shape: per-vertex position and normal deltas added to the base
// mesh, scaled by the target's weight. Both delta arrays are parallel to the
// mesh's vertices; an empty NormalDeltas array means "positions only".
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morph_target_animation)
type MorphTarget
    implements IValue
{
    Name: String;
    PositionDeltas: Array<Vector3D>;
    NormalDeltas: Array<Vector3D>;
}

// The activation weights of a mesh's morph targets, parallel to its target
// array. Weights are nominally in [0, 1]; values outside exaggerate or invert
// a target.
type MorphWeights
    implements IValue
{
    Values: Array<Proportion>;
}

// A named socket on a bone for attaching props and accessories. Offset places
// the socket relative to the bone.
type BoneSocket
    implements IValue
{
    Name: String;
    Bone: BoneIndex;
    Offset: Pose3D;
}

// A skeletal animation clip: one transform track per bone, parallel to the
// target skeleton's bone array, plus trigger events. Track values are local
// (parent-relative) transforms.
type SkeletalClip
    implements IValue
{
    Name: String;
    Duration: Duration;
    BoneTracks: Array<TransformTrack3D>;
    Events: Array<AnimationEvent>;
}

//==
// # IProcedural rig control
//
// The structures that adjust a skeleton's pose rather than store it:
// inverse-kinematics chains and their goals, aim and twist constraints,
// per-bone masking of an animation layer, and the bone mapping that retargets
// a clip from one skeleton onto another. Bone references index the owning
// skeleton's bone array; -1 is the "no bone" sentinel throughout.

// The algorithm an inverse-kinematics chain is solved with: an analytic
// two-segment solve, cyclic coordinate descent, or forward-and-backward
// reaching.
type IkSolver = TwoBone | Ccd | Fabrik;

// The goal of an inverse-kinematics solve: where the chain's end effector
// should be and how it should be oriented. The two weights blend the solved
// result over the input pose per goal component.
type IkTarget
    implements IValue
{
    Position: Point3D;
    Orientation: Quaternion;
    PositionWeight: Proportion;
    OrientationWeight: Proportion;
}
```
